// ==== GeneratedValidatorRegistration.g.cs ====
// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable

namespace Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection {
    using global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions;
    using global::ValidationModules;
    using global::ValidationModules.Naming;

    /// <summary>Registers every validator this assembly generated.</summary>
    public static class GeneratorTestsValidationExtensions {

        /// <summary>
        /// Adds this assembly's generated validators, and a validation runner for each
        /// validated type.
        /// </summary>
        /// <remarks>
        /// <b>Not idempotent.</b> Calling this twice registers every validator twice, and a
        /// runner merges every registered validator for a type - so each error would be
        /// reported twice. Add rather than TryAdd is deliberate: registering a second
        /// validator for one type is how a hand-written rule composes with the generated
        /// one, so this cannot dedupe without breaking that.
        /// </remarks>
        public static IServiceCollection AddGeneratorTestsValidators(this IServiceCollection services) {
            services.AddSingleton<IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Address>, global::Sample.AddressValidator>();
            services.AddSingleton<IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Pet>, global::Sample.PetValidator>();

            services.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Address>();
            services.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Pet>();

            // TryAdd, so a namer the consumer registered first survives. The policy here is
            // the one the literals above were emitted with, so the engines that resolve a
            // namer at run time agree with the generated code by default.
            services.TryAddSingleton<IValidationFieldNamer>(CamelCaseFieldNamer.Instance);

            return services;
        }
    }
}


// ==== Sample.AddressValidator.g.cs ====
// <auto-generated/>
#nullable enable

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using ValidationModules;

namespace Sample;

public sealed partial class AddressValidator : IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Address> {

    public AddressValidator() { }

    public void Validate(ref ValidationContext ctx, global::Sample.Address value) {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value.Street)) ctx.AddRequired("street");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The same tests as <see cref="Validate"/>, returning at the first failure and building
    /// no path, message or error record - a caller wanting only a boolean pays for nothing else.
    /// </summary>
    public bool IsValid(global::Sample.Address value) {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value.Street)) return false;
        return true;
    }
}
